page.layout: One page of text: a title block at top centre, then a verse poem with a large woodcut initial at left, a closing signature line in italic beside the poem's end, and a signature mark "IN" at lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.head: In Historiam Frisicam
CLARISSIMI VIRI DOMINI PIERII WINSEMII, IC. Ordinum Frisiae Historiographi & Historiarum atque Eloquentiae Professoris, inter operas Typographicas, ante editum opus, defuncti.
main_text.p: DNVIDA mors nulli mortali parcere docta, Saepius egregios, suspiciosa, premens, Viderat hunc prodire librum, qui reddaret ævum Exstinctis longo tempore funeribus. Qui Soli exhibeat res gestas luce Carentum Lethe devicta, Tartareoque specu.
main_text.l: Scilicet hic veterum patrata leguntur avorum,
Quos tenet inferni regia muta poli.
WINSHEMI calamus duxit de nocte profundâ
Quotquot in Hispanos animosi ivêre secures,
Et soboli dederunt libera regna suæ.
Sic quicunque, inquit, mortem violare deinde
Speret & è Stygia victor abire domo.
Sic invisè jaces, solâ tamen utere vitâ,
Quam potuit functis addere docta manus.
Ergo parte sui subijt WINSEMIUS umbras,
Et non emissum morte reliquit opus:
Parte sui meliore viget, vivetque per illos,
Quibus tribuit nunquam posse deinde mori.

page.notes: The initial "D" is a large woodcut letter, joined to "NVIDA" as "DNVIDA". The first line's small capitals are rendered as printed. Some words in the poem are uncertain due to the scan, notably "Pieridum", "Lethe", and "Quibus". The closing name line is in italic with spaced capitals. The poem is set as verse lines; the printed indentation was not reproduced exactly.
